slides.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents
slides.tldr: CONTROLLABLE OPINION DYNAMICS IN LLM AGENTS
slides.highlight: Introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents to separate belief from speech, enabling controllable opinion dynamics and auditable simulations for MIMIC's societal-scale agent modeling.

card.one_liner: Bayesian Chronicle Agents use an explicit belief layer to make LLM social simulations controllable and auditable.
card.key_idea: A Bayesian update layer separates belief from speech, using a prior-strength parameter (κ) to control stubbornness and replicate classical opinion dynamics regimes (consensus, disagreement, minority influence).
card.evaluation: Tested on four LLMs using synthetic policy questions; validated via Spearman rank-order recovery of κ and R² (0.93–0.99) against Friedkin–Johnsen fixed points.
card.limitation: Limited to one synthetic topic, binary stances, and small populations (N=20) on complete graphs, not predicting real human opinion change.

slides.title: SocioVerse2: A Longitudinal Dynamic Social Simulation Framework under a Human-AI Co-evolutionary Paradigm
slides.highlight: SocioVerse2 introduces a human-AI co-evolutionary paradigm for longitudinal social simulation, supporting the meso- and societal-scale impact analysis central to MIMIC.

card.one_liner: SocioVerse2 is a social simulation framework enabling longitudinal experiments via human-AI co-evolutionary research loops.
card.key_idea: It combines a longitudinal simulation loop for counterfactual branching/interventions with a controllable research loop for human-steered state editing, supported by a skill-based agentic infrastructure.
card.evaluation: Validated across three case families and seven studies, including reproducing ABMs, policy modeling, and macro-economic index nowcasting using real-world grounding.

slides.title: MSI-Bench: Evaluating Multi-Speaker Voice Interaction for Collaborative AI Agents
slides.highlight: This work introduces MSI-Bench to evaluate multi-speaker voice interaction, identifying critical gaps in speaker-grounded perception and conversational restraint. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: MSI-Bench evaluates AI voice agents' ability to handle multi-speaker memory, instruction following, and reasoning.
card.key_idea: A bilingual benchmark of 1,152 scripted audio scenes testing speaker-grounded perception, authority constraints, selective disclosure, and conversational restraint using atomic rubrics and tool-call validation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 12 models (e.g., Gemini, GPT, Qwen) using APR, ARS, and tool execution metrics; results validated via human study (82.6% judge agreement).
card.limitation: Uses synthesized, scripted speech and lacks positive cases for selective engagement during bystander interjections.

slides.title: Identity Continuity in Long-Term Embodied AI Relationships: From Agent-Specific Identity Representation to Identity-Continuity Appraisal
slides.tldr: FRAMEWORK FOR IDENTITY CONTINUITY IN EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: This paper proposes a framework for maintaining identity continuity in long-term embodied AI through perceptual, behavioral, and autobiographical domains, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A framework for maintaining perceived identity continuity in long-term embodied AI despite system updates or migrations.
card.key_idea: Identity is represented via three weighted domains: embodied-perceptual, psychological-behavioral, and relational-autobiographical, which users integrate to judge if a changed agent remains the same.

slides.title: LLM-based Conversational AI Knowledge Assistant for MyBuddy Humanoid Robot
slides.tldr: LLM-POWERED CONVERSATIONAL ASSISTANT FOR HUMANOID ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work implements an LLM-based assistant for a humanoid robot to enable natural, context-aware interaction and knowledge retrieval, supporting the RwB goal of enhancing embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: An LLM-based conversational assistant for the MyBuddy humanoid robot enabling real-time, knowledge-rich speech interactions.
card.key_idea: A cascading speech-to-speech architecture integrating Whisper-Fast (ASR), Llama 3.1 8B via Agno agent with internet tool-calling (Wikipedia, arXiv), and Kokoro-82M (TTS).
card.evaluation: Qualitative dialogue experiments on diverse topics and quantitative measurement of LLM execution times (ranging from 12s to 42s).
card.limitation: Response latency depends on query complexity and external tool usage; requires a GPU-driven PC for optimal performance.

slides.title: MIRA: Real-Time Full-Duplex Human-Robot Interaction for Embodied Companions
slides.highlight: MIRA introduces a unified framework for full-duplex interaction that synchronizes streaming speech with expressive, interruptible motions, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: MIRA enables real-time, full-duplex human-robot interaction with synchronized streaming speech and interruptible co-speech motion.
card.key_idea: CORTEX manages turn-taking and routes responses to either discrete behavior libraries or ROSCO, a prefix-conditioned diffusion model generating streaming motion via Receding-Horizon Prefix Commitment.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the BEAT dataset and Astribot S1 humanoid; demonstrated competitive audio-motion alignment and effective real-robot barge-in handling.

slides.title: Gaze as Evidence for Common Grounding: A Cross-Corpus Analysis of MapTask and MUNDEX
slides.tldr: GAZE AS A CUE FOR COMMON GROUNDING
slides.highlight: This research analyzes how gaze features, such as gaze entropy and task-directed gaze, correlate with grounding and reference alignment in collaborative tasks. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement within human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Gaze patterns provide consistent, though modest, evidence of grounding across two distinct asymmetric collaborative tasks.
card.key_idea: Mapped MapTask and MUNDEX gaze annotations to a shared partner/task/away vocabulary to analyze associations between gaze features and grounding states.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via Mann-Whitney U tests, GEE, and logistic regression (macro-F1) using grouped cross-validation on MapTask and MUNDEX corpora.
card.limitation: Small effect sizes, limited participant groups, and sensitivity to inference units limit the generalizability of the predictive results.

slides.title: Object-Centered Reconstruction for Vision-Based 3D Force Estimation
slides.highlight: This work proposes a vision-based pipeline to estimate 3D interaction forces from soft-tissue deformation, supporting MOSAIC's focus on physics and force-based human proficiency estimation.

card.one_liner: A vision-based pipeline estimating 3D interaction forces from soft-tissue deformation in stereo endoscopic video.
card.key_idea: Reconstructs tissue point clouds in an object-centered coordinate frame, tracks points using geometry-constrained SIREN optimization, and regresses force via a Set Transformer and LSTM.
card.evaluation: Tested on rubber-glove phantoms and ex vivo porcine colons using RMSE and R². Achieved average RMSEs of 0.77N and 1.30N, respectively.
card.limitation: End-to-end speed is limited to 1 FPS due to depth estimation; object-frame definition assumes long, tubular anatomy.

slides.title: Partner-Specific Affective Precision in Social Active Inference
slides.highlight: This work introduces affective precision as a relationship-specific metacognitive estimate of confidence, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and adapting to different partners in human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Proposes relationship-specific affective precision to decouple social prediction from policy commitment in multi-agent active inference.
card.key_idea: A metacognitive confidence signal, derived from partner-response predictability (surprisal) rather than payoff, modulates policy precision to sharpen or flatten commitment for each specific partner.
card.evaluation: Simulated in a multi-partner graded trust game using pymdp; compared full precision against shared-beta, tracked-only, and no-affect ablations via policy entropy and payoff.
card.limitation: Confidence is an auxiliary tracker, meaning it can lag behind abrupt social changes as the agent lacks explicit stale-confidence detection.

slides.title: ABM-SIRTEM: A Hybrid Agent-Based and Epidemiological Model for Pandemic Response
slides.highlight: This work proposes a hybrid model integrating individual-level socioeconomic factors and compliance dynamics, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: ABM-SIRTEM is a hybrid model coupling population-level disease dynamics with agent-based socioeconomic behavior and compliance.
card.key_idea: It integrates SIRTEM epidemiological compartments with an ABM where agent compliance evolves via evolutionary game theory based on economic productivity, mental well-being, and health risks.
card.evaluation: Calibrated using Bayesian optimization against historical COVID-19 positive/negative test counts from four U.S. states; results show broad reproduction of infection waves.
card.limitation: The evaluation assesses calibration fit rather than predictive performance on held-out data.

slides.title: Inferring the microscopic mechanisms of opinion dynamics using a kinetic Ising model
slides.tldr: EMPIRICAL VALIDATION OF KINETIC ISING MODELS FOR OPINION DYNAMICS
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that kinetic Ising models can accurately describe online opinion formation by linking microscopic social behaviors to network topology, supporting the agent-based modeling goals of MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Empirical evidence from Twitter climate debates validates kinetic Ising models for describing binary opinion dynamics.
card.key_idea: Inferred transition probabilities from a year-long social network using a hierarchy of kinetic Ising models, incorporating social influence, intrinsic bias, and degree-dependent temporal persistence.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using log-loss on weekly fits and Monte Carlo simulations. Results accurately reproduced empirical response functions, flip probabilities, and macroscopic opinion trajectories.
card.limitation: The analysis identifies correlations between network topology and opinion persistence but does not establish the direction of causality.

slides.title: Toward Human-in-the-Loop Robot Failure Recovery: Bridging Communication Gaps in Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.highlight: This work introduces LD-HRI to evaluate how robots can better communicate with humans of varying knowledge levels during failure recovery, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: LD-HRI is a benchmark evaluating robot help requests across controlled expert and novice listener knowledge levels.
card.key_idea: A web-based communication game and dataset manipulating control-interface, robot-part, and scene information to measure how listener knowledge gaps affect failure recovery success.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 1,302 human listener trials (446 human requests) and 560 trials (24 LLM requests) using task success and NASA-TLX workload.
card.limitation: Does not establish a causal advantage between human and LLM speakers; results are descriptive across different task structures.

slides.title: Designing Against Deskilling: Metacognitive Feedback Reduces Cognitive Offloading to LLM Assistants
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates that metacognitive feedback can reduce cognitive offloading to LLMs and improve user performance, supporting ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and meta-cognition in human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Metacognitive feedback reduces cognitive offloading to LLM assistants and improves subsequent unaided skill performance.
card.key_idea: Comparing metacognitive feedback (making offloading implications explicit) and effort-based rewards (incentivizing less AI help) to prevent deskilling during fraction arithmetic practice.
card.evaluation: Preregistered online experiment (N=704) using a 2x2-plus-control design; measured answer offloading and unaided test scores. Results were statistically significant for feedback.
card.limitation: The study focused on a specific mathematical task (fraction arithmetic), which may not generalize to all skill types.

slides.title: Voice-Light: A Full-Duplex Cascaded Voice Agent with Causal Turn-Taking and Speculative Generation
slides.tldr: FULL-DUPLEX VOICE AGENT WITH CAUSAL TURN-TAKING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a voice agent capable of handling overlaps and speculative generation, contributing to HyECHO's goals regarding addressee/listener modeling and engagement in human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: A full-duplex voice agent using speculative generation and a shared-encoder adapter for causal turn-taking.
card.key_idea: Combines a causal adapter sharing Nemotron ASR features with private speculative generation and a hybrid controller to manage reversible playback and audible-only conversation history.
card.evaluation: Locked test on 1,673 silence candidates; 36-turn operator case study. Learned policy failed to beat Silero timing baselines in EOT recall.
card.limitation: Learned turn-taking adapter transferred poorly from synthetic to human data and was not evaluated on locked test sets.

slides.title: Towards Reliable Underwater Diver-Robot Interaction: Gesture Design, Interaction Logic, and Real-World Evaluation
slides.highlight: This research proposes a gesture-based interaction framework for underwater robots, focusing on gesture recognizability and command-level logic to reduce errors. It is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: A closed-loop framework for reliable underwater diver-robot interaction using a seven-gesture vocabulary and interaction logic.
card.key_idea: Combines lightweight landmark-based KNN recognition with command-level logic (Hold-based authorization and temporal confirmation) to mitigate visual similarity and transient recognition errors during robot execution.
card.evaluation: User study (30 participants) and physical robot experiments in a tank and swimming pool. Achieved 88.17% command accuracy and 77.42% task success rate.
card.limitation: Temporal confirmation introduces response latency and may reject brief valid gestures; broader evaluation across diverse divers and conditions is needed.

slides.title: Xingyuan Intelligence Demonstrates Embodied Brain's Cross-Ontology Capability
slides.highlight: Xingyuan Intelligence demonstrated a cross-ontology embodied brain through multi-robot collaborative rope skipping, offering insights for RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction.

slides.title: Google Launches DeepMind Institute on AGI Safety and Expands AI Agent CC
slides.highlight: The expansion of AI agents for family coordination relates to ADAM-CHAT's focus on adaptive AI teammates and human-AI teaming.

slides.title: Chinese Startup Spirit AI Predicts Humanoid Robots Following Verbal Commands by Mid-2027
slides.highlight: Spirit AI anticipates the arrival of humanoid robots capable of following verbal commands by mid-2027, relating to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

slides.title: CE$^4$L: Continual Ego, Exo, and Ego-Exo Learning
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for continual learning across ego and exo views, addressing cross-view correspondence and skill assessment relevant to the MOSAIC project's focus on ego-exo views.

card.one_liner: CE4L is a multi-view continual learning benchmark for embodied agents with a competitive adapter-based baseline.
card.key_idea: VISTA uses lightweight task-specific adapters and a training-free router that assigns tasks based on residual distances to whitened subspaces derived from second-order statistics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on four tasks (skill assessment, segmentation, association, anticipation/planning) using EgoExoLearn; VISTA achieved state-of-the-art overall performance against representative CL baselines.

slides.title: Affective Shared Autonomy: Temporal Affect Dynamics and Subjective Evaluation in Bimanual Teleoperation Tasks
slides.highlight: This work proposes a framework that modulates robotic assistance based on real-time operator affective states, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: An affect-aware shared autonomy framework for bimanual teleoperation that modulates robotic assistance based on real-time operator states.
card.key_idea: A multimodal fusion model (facial video, cardiac signals, arm kinematics) estimates affective states to trigger assistance only during sustained adverse states, preserving user agency.
card.evaluation: User study (N=30) across three modes. Metrics included annotated state proportions and NASA-TLX surveys. Proposed model outperformed zero-shot baselines in state tracking.
card.limitation: Personalized affective models require iterative calibration; time-constrained trials limited full co-adaptation, causing mild unpredictability and slightly lower satisfaction than static assistance.

slides.title: Simultaneous Forward and Inverse Human-in-the-Loop Optimization
slides.highlight: This work introduces SFIHILO to efficiently infer individual-specific reward functions and optimize control policies, supporting the development of personalized human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: SFIHILO efficiently infers individual human reward functions and optimizes robot control policies using active querying.
card.key_idea: Jointly learns a forward policy-to-outcome model and an inverse outcome-to-reward model, using a 'Boundary Lookahead' acquisition function to reduce uncertainty near preference boundaries.
card.evaluation: Simulated 30 heterogeneous users; compared against Random and Mutual Information querying. Results showed significantly higher sample efficiency and robustness to dimensionality and noise.
card.limitation: Not yet validated in physical human trials; performance depends on the correct selection of outcome features.

slides.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
slides.tldr: DUAL-PROCESS AGENTS WITH MEMORY AND SELF-REFLECTION
slides.highlight: This work introduces an Adaptive Memory Module and a Self-Reflection Module to improve state tracking and corrective intervention, supporting ADAM-CHAT's goals of self-monitoring and meta-cognition for adaptive agents.

card.one_liner: Dual-process language agents improve in interactive environments by combining episodic memory with bounded self-reflection.
card.key_idea: Extends SwiftSage with an Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) for salience-gated episodic storage and a Self-Reflection Module (SRM) for execution-time validation and trigger-gated corrective intervention.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on ScienceWorld; full system achieved highest mean final score (64.62) and success rate (43.17%) compared to baseline and single-module ablations.
card.limitation: Memory is primarily episodic without semantic consolidation; SRM relies on hand-crafted thresholds and shallow deterministic repairs.

slides.authors: João Meneses dos Santos et al.
